items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: I think Red Saunders taught us a little about the hard time that he had trying even to put a hall together

ctx.x: And the Depression. And with radio, big bands sound good on radio, little bands don't sound so

good. So they stopped. The big band with the fullness of it. And so we were slowly -- and Louis Armstrong wasn't -- tried doing it by himself and he has having a hard time. I think Red Saunders taught us a little about the hard time that he had trying even to put a hall together and rent a hall and do something to keep his way of life.

items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: I went down with Art Hodes.

ctx.x: And we find it so different, and when I was down in New Orleans here in '68, I was at the first jazz festival they had. I went down with Art Hodes.
